title: Unvisited work cells retain their contents
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $\tau$ be a work-tape index, let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$, and let $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ with $a\le b$. Suppose that at every time $r$ with $a\le r<b$, the head of work tape $\tau$ is not at cell $p$ during the run of $M$ on $x$. Then the contents of cell $p$ on that tape after $b$ steps equal its contents after $a$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
At every time $r$ with $a\le r<b$, the selected tape head is not at $p$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes whose cells are indexed by
$\mathbb{Z}$, let $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, $\tau \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, $p \in \mathbb{Z}$, and
let $a \le b$ be natural numbers. If for every $r$ with $a \le r < b$ the head of work tape
$\tau$ is not at cell $p$ after $r$ steps of $M$ on $x$, then the content of cell $p$ of
work tape $\tau$ after $b$ steps of $M$ on $x$ equals its content after $a$ steps.
